source: Windows PowerShell parser and in-memory ScheduledTasks triggers

# At 09:00 every day, starting 2026-11-14. Times are the computer's local time.
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At '2026-11-14T09:00:00'
# New-ScheduledTaskTrigger stores -At as UTC, which pins the trigger to UTC and moves it by an hour across DST changes.
# Writing the start boundary without an offset keeps it at the same local time all year.
$trigger.StartBoundary = '2026-11-14T09:00:00'

# Template: replace the values in angle brackets, review, then run these lines yourself.

# At 00:00 every day, starting 2026-11-14. After triggered, repeat every 15 minutes for a duration of 1 day. Times are the computer's local time.
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At '2026-11-14T00:00:00'
# New-ScheduledTaskTrigger stores -At as UTC, which pins the trigger to UTC and moves it by an hour across DST changes.
# Writing the start boundary without an offset keeps it at the same local time all year.
$trigger.StartBoundary = '2026-11-14T00:00:00'
# Daily and weekly triggers take no repetition parameters; copy the repetition from a one-time trigger.
$trigger.Repetition = (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At '2026-11-14T00:00:00' -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 15) -RepetitionDuration (New-TimeSpan -Days 1)).Repetition
# Do not stop a run that is still going when the repetition duration ends (the cmdlet turns this on).
$trigger.Repetition.StopAtDurationEnd = $false
